title: VMware in Plain English: ESXi, vCenter and Clusters
summary: Build the basic mental model for ESXi hosts, vCenter inventory and cluster services before operating production workloads.
plain_language_explanation: ESXi runs virtual machines on physical hosts. vCenter provides centralized inventory, policy and orchestration. A cluster groups hosts so services such as HA, DRS and vMotion can coordinate availability, placement and maintenance.
quick_check: Why should vCenter health and ESXi host health be checked separately during an incident?

title: vSphere Architecture, Inventory and Control Boundaries
summary: Operate ESXi and vCenter as distinct layers with explicit inventory, networking, storage and management dependencies.
objective: Explain how vCenter, ESXi hosts, clusters, virtual switches, datastores and management dependencies interact without treating the control plane as the workload plane.
body_outline: Separate vCenter availability from ESXi host and VM availability.
Maintain authoritative inventory of clusters, hosts, datastores, networks and VM ownership.
Treat management networking, vMotion networking and workload networking as separate failure domains.
Treat storage connectivity and datastore accessibility as prerequisites for many cluster operations.
Understand that moving a host between vCenter systems can require recreation or revalidation of HA, DRS and distributed-switch configuration.
Use provider evidence before assuming an inventory or agent problem is a compute failure.

title: vSphere HA, DRS and vMotion Operating Model
summary: Understand what HA, DRS and vMotion actually do, their dependencies and where automation can be constrained.
objective: Separate availability restart behavior, resource-placement decisions and live migration so operators diagnose the correct cluster service.
body_outline: vSphere HA focuses on recovery/restart behavior after host or VM availability failures; it is not a load balancer.
DRS evaluates placement and migration benefit subject to rules, compatibility and resource constraints; a visually uneven cluster can still be healthy.
vMotion moves running VMs between compatible hosts and can briefly stun sensitive workloads.
Admission control, VM/Host rules, reservations, compatibility and network health can change DRS or HA behavior.
Concurrent migration limits can queue vMotion and provisioning operations instead of indicating an immediate failure.
Maintenance operations require an evacuation strategy before remediation can succeed.

title: vSphere Lifecycle and Cluster Change Assurance
summary: Design patch and lifecycle work around desired-state images, maintenance prerequisites and post-change cluster validation.
architecture_notes: vSphere Lifecycle Manager image-based management defines desired host state across ESX/ESXi version, add-ons and supported firmware/driver components. Remediation still depends on safe maintenance-mode entry, VM evacuation, cluster capacity and compatible networking/storage. Post-change validation must prove host connectivity, HA/DRS state, datastore/network access and VM service health rather than treating a completed patch task as sufficient evidence.
failure_modes: host cannot enter maintenance mode because workloads cannot be evacuated
DRS cannot select a compatible destination because rules or resource constraints block placement
vMotion queues because migration concurrency limits are saturated
post-vCenter update HA agents reconfigure and are misread as permanent cluster failure
firmware and driver combinations drift from supported desired state
maintenance succeeds but network or datastore reachability is degraded afterward
enterprise_design_notes: Use staged maintenance windows, capacity headroom, image compliance evidence, vendor compatibility checks, rollback criteria and explicit post-change service validation.

title: Read-Only vSphere Cluster and Lifecycle Evidence Pack
summary: Collect vCenter, host, cluster, DRS, HA, datastore and lifecycle evidence without changing production state.
objective: Produce a timestamped vSphere evidence pack before any HA, DRS, migration or lifecycle change is proposed.
steps: Confirm the approved vCenter, datacenter, cluster and host scope.
Record vCenter and ESX/ESXi version/build information and connection state.
Inventory HA and DRS enabled state, admission-control summary and active VM/Host rules.
Inventory host maintenance state, VM placement, datastore accessibility and relevant network objects.
Review lifecycle/compliance status without starting remediation.
Classify findings as control-plane, compute, placement, network, storage or lifecycle issues before recommending change.
expected_result: A read-only evidence pack describing cluster membership, placement, availability settings, storage/network visibility and lifecycle state without mutation.
rollback: Not required; prescribed activities are read-only.

title: vSphere Cluster, vMotion or Remediation Failure Decision Tree
summary: Separate control-plane, compatibility, rule, capacity, networking, storage and lifecycle failure domains before changing cluster state.
diagnostic_order: Confirm vCenter connectivity, target cluster/host and exact operation before interpreting symptoms.
For DRS or vMotion issues, check compatibility, VM/Host rules, reservations/admission constraints, migration concurrency, network path and datastore accessibility.
For maintenance/remediation failures, prove workload evacuation and destination capacity before retrying lifecycle work.
For HA anomalies after vCenter update, distinguish expected agent reconfiguration from persistent cluster failure.
For sensitive workloads, account for vMotion stun behavior before assuming migration is risk-free.
Escalate when remediation requires host maintenance mode, migration, lifecycle remediation, HA/DRS policy changes or reboot.
escalation_boundary: Do not enter maintenance mode, migrate workloads, change HA/DRS rules, remediate hosts, modify distributed switches/datastores or reboot ESX/ESXi hosts without approved change authority.

title: VMware Foundations and Operations Assessment
summary: Scenario assessment covering architecture, HA/DRS/vMotion and lifecycle evidence.

assessment_items.question: Does an uneven-looking cluster prove DRS is malfunctioning?
assessment_items.answer: No. DRS evaluates the benefit and cost of migrations together with rules, compatibility and resource state. A visually uneven cluster can still have acceptable DRS scores.

assessment_items.question: Why can Lifecycle Manager remediation stall before patching starts?
assessment_items.answer: The host may be unable to enter maintenance mode because running workloads cannot be evacuated automatically or safely.

assessment_items.question: Why should HA behavior and DRS behavior be diagnosed separately?
assessment_items.answer: HA is primarily concerned with availability recovery, while DRS focuses on placement and resource balancing. They have different triggers and constraints.

assessment_items.question: What must be validated after host lifecycle work?
assessment_items.answer: Host connection, cluster HA/DRS state, datastore and network access, VM placement and actual workload health.

title: Senior VMware Interview: Cluster Resilience, Mobility and Lifecycle
summary: Senior scenarios testing evidence-first diagnosis of HA, DRS, vMotion and ESXi lifecycle behavior.

questions.question: DRS leaves one host nearly empty. What do you inspect before forcing migrations?
Lifecycle remediation will not start on a cluster host. What is your sequence?
answer_points: define downtime path for unmovable workloads

questions.question: What risks can exist even when vMotion succeeds technically?
How do you distinguish expected HA reconfiguration after vCenter upgrade from a real HA outage?
answer_points: validate cluster HA health after stabilization
